ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR diluted share counts are in ordinary shares while the Nasdaq price is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x8 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price
ads_ratio.source: Futu Holdings Limited Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (filed 2025-04-14), Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Note 1 (General Information, Organization and Principal Activities): each American Depositary Share represents eight Class A ordinary shares; the same statement appears in the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-15)

base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (broker-dealer): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is client-balance plumbing, not distributable earnings (FY2025 OCF $5,240,468,000 vs net income $1,456,671,000; FY2023 OCF -$811,352,000 vs net income $548,140,000), so it is rejected as the base (IBKR precedent in this sweep). For a broker, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy: SBC is already expensed inside it, and FY2025 capex ($7,033,000) and D&A ($9,291,000) are trivial and roughly offset. Latest-FY net income is used over the 3-yr median NI per ADS ($5.00, the FY2024 figure) because the median averages in the pre-inflection client base; the FY2025 base is still below the ex-penalty 2026 interim run-rate reported in the company's 6-K releases (see analysis.md).
base_override.source: financials_history.csv (this run's engine-filed USD figures): FY2025 net income $1,456,671,000 / diluted shares 1,130,846,701 = $1.2881 per ordinary share, scaled x8 ordinary shares per ADS (ads_ratio) = $10.3050 per ADS

moat_against: Retail brokerage switching costs are low — Webull, Tiger/UP Fintech, Robinhood and local brokers/banks contest every market Futu enters

China regulatory franchise is impaired, not protected: mainland onboarding barred since late 2022, app removed from mainland app stores in 2023, and the May 2026 CSRC pre-notification proposed ~RMB1.85B in confiscation and fines over unlicensed mainland business (~13% of Futu Securities funded accounts were mainland-related)
Earnings are geared to trading volumes and interest rates — Q2 2026's record volume is a market-activity print, not a run-rate
Founder dual-class control (Leaf Hua Li) and VIE structure; US securities class action followed the CSRC disclosure
International expansion is bought with rising CAC (~HK$2,600 blended in Q2 2026, within the company's HK$2.5k-3.0k guidance) and marketing spend in markets where Futu has no incumbent brand
moat_for: Dominant Hong Kong retail brokerage franchise (Futubull) plus a scaling moomoo network across Singapore, Malaysia, the US, Australia, Japan and Canada — 3.84M funded accounts (+33.6% YoY) and HK$1.40T client assets (+43.6% YoY) at Q2 2026
Tech-platform cost structure: gross margin 82.0-87.1% over FY2023-2025 (fundamentals.json) and FY2025 operating margin 61.6% on the filer's total-revenue basis

Returns on equity rose 17.4% (FY2023) to 19.4% (FY2024) to 28.3% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json, with the roic_proxy series at 21.7% / 34.4% / 39.5% over the same years (proxy denominator excludes client balances — see analysis.md)

Diversifying revenue: brokerage commissions, margin/securities-lending interest, FX and IPO financing, wealth/fund distribution and new products (US prediction markets, virtual-asset margin financing in Hong Kong)
Product/community flywheel: 31.3M registered users and an in-app investor community that lowers organic acquisition cost in its home market
moat_justification: A real but narrow franchise moat: Hong Kong's leading retail broker with a proprietary tech platform, 82-87% gross margins and ROE rising to 28.3% in FY2025, scaling internationally — but retail switching costs are low, the historic mainland-China growth channel has been closed and penalized by the CSRC, and earnings ride trading volumes and rates. The measured returns are strong but substantially earned in a volume boom and the roic_proxy denominator excludes the client balances that fund the balance sheet, so the score sits at moderate, not strong.
name: Futu Holdings Ltd
one_liner: Leading Hong Kong online broker (Futubull/moomoo), moat 5/10 — on a corrected net-income base of $10.30 per ADS (the engine's OCF base is client-balance plumbing and prints a fake Tier S) it clears 15% (weighted IRR 20.2%, weighted IV@15% $159.12 vs the $105.64 price), but the finance-sector model misfit, a bear-C to bull-S tier band and a Tier C result on the median-NI base cap confidence at low — size it to the bear end (bear IV@15% $95.54).
